title: Modelibr - private asset library now with MCP
author: papyszoo
selftext:
Hey,

For some time now I am working on Modelibr - self hosted (docker or installable) game asset library. I just released a v0.6 version and I added MCP support with experimental scene building with AI agent. It's a first version and results are mixed but I'll keep improving this feature - especially with your feedback.

If you want to see how installed app looks like you can go here: [https://modelibr.com/demo/](https://modelibr.com/demo/)

Please keep in mind that app is still in development and some features are experimental.

I would love to hear your ideas and if you encounter any bugs please let me know.

comments.author: CharacterTension2896
comments.body: What is this for or what does it do

replies.author: papyszoo
replies.body:
It's for you to organize your assets. You install it on your pc (or home server if you have one) and you can access it in your network with your browser.

Personally I use it to track models I create so I have visual feedback (animated thumbnail + you can open model in browser).

But I also added textures support, sounds, sprites, env maps and I keep adding features. With MCP added you can just point your agent at a directory on your disk if you have some assets there and it will process those and add to Modelibr so you can keep everything organized.

With scene building you have now precise description of each asset so agent can pick best one that matches your project and create a scene out of it.

replies.author: papyszoo
replies.body:
Should be fine but depending on complexity of your assets and how many of them you have it may take a while to process them. To generate each thumbnail it is rendering each asset multiple times to create animation out of it.

And if you're not using it you can just close it.
